unit.title: Follow principles of Occupational Health and Safety (OH&S) in work environment

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is a "hazard"?
options: The chance that someone will be hurt by something
A form that is filled in after an accident
Anything that could cause harm, such as a live wire
The safety officer who checks the workshop

questions.stem: What is "risk"?
options: Any tool or machine that is used in the workshop
How likely harm is, and how bad it could be
The list of safety rules on the notice board
The name of the person who reports accidents

questions.stem: Which of these is a hazard you might find in a welding shop or an electrical lab?
options: A frayed power cable lying across a walkway
A fire extinguisher hung on its bracket
A first aid kit that has been fully stocked
A clear, well-lit walkway with no clutter

questions.stem: Which control is the most effective way to deal with a hazard?
options: Giving workers PPE to wear
Putting up a warning sign
Training workers to take care
Removing the hazard altogether

questions.stem: In the order of controls, where does PPE come?
options: Last, after other controls have been used
First, before any other kind of control is tried
Only after an accident has happened
It is not part of the order of controls

questions.stem: What are the main steps of a risk assessment?
options: Buy PPE for everyone, start the job and then see what happens
Wait for an accident, then write a report on it
Ask the customer, then follow what they say
Find hazards, judge the risk, control it, record and review

questions.stem: When grinding steel, which PPE protects the eyes and face best?
options: Dark sunglasses from a shop
A paper dust mask over the nose
Safety glasses with a face shield
A cap with a long peak pulled down low

questions.stem: Why must PPE be checked before each use?
options: To make sure it is the newest colour
Damaged PPE may not protect you
So that it can be signed out to a friend
Because it must be washed every hour

questions.stem: When should ear protection be worn in a workshop?
options: Only when the supervisor is in the room to see you
Only when you are working outdoors
Only when the radio is playing
When noise is loud, such as grinding or cutting

questions.stem: What does a red circle with a red line across a picture mean?
options: That action is not allowed
You must do that action
There is a hazard somewhere nearby
The way to a fire exit

questions.stem: What colour are safe condition signs, such as first aid and emergency exit signs?
options: Red
Green
Yellow
Blue

questions.stem: What three things make up the fire triangle?
options: Smoke, flame and ash
Water, wind and sand
Heat, fuel and oxygen
Sparks, wood and paper

questions.stem: Which extinguisher is suitable for a fire in live electrical equipment?
options: A bucket of water
Carbon dioxide (CO2)
Water-based foam
A wet cloth or blanket

questions.stem: Why must water never be used on a fire involving live electrical equipment?
options: It makes the fire smell much worse
It costs too much to use water
Water conducts electricity and can cause a shock
Water takes far too long to reach the fire from the tap

questions.stem: What is the first thing to do if you find a fire that is too big to put out?
options: Collect your tools and your bag
Finish the job you are working on
Open all the windows and doors to let the smoke escape
Raise the alarm and leave by the nearest safe exit

questions.stem: Where should you go when the building is evacuated?
options: To the agreed assembly point
To your car in the car park
Back inside to collect your phone and bag
To the toilets to hide

questions.stem: Before working on an electrical circuit, what is the safe order of steps?
options: Test it with your finger, then switch off
Switch off at the socket, then start work
Switch off, lock off, tag, then prove dead with a tester
Ask a co-worker to stand and hold the switch off while you work

questions.stem: Why must a voltage tester be checked on a known live source before and after testing a circuit?
options: To make sure the tester is working, so the result can be trusted
To charge the tester's battery so that it will last longer on the job
To make the tester read a higher voltage
Because the law says the tester must be warm

questions.stem: A co-worker is getting an electric shock and is still touching the equipment. What should you do first?
options: Pull them away with your bare hands
Throw water over them straight away to cool them down
Run to find a first aid book
Switch off the power at the switch or isolator

questions.stem: How should a minor burn be treated first?
options: Rub butter, oil or toothpaste onto the burn
Hold it under cool running water for 20 minutes
Burst any blisters with a clean needle straight away
Wrap it in fluffy cotton wool and leave it for a day

questions.stem: What should you do if you use the last bandage from the first aid kit?
options: Tell the person in charge so that it is restocked
Keep quiet about it, because someone else will notice later
Take another kit home in case you need it
Use tape and paper towels from now on

questions.stem: What is a "near miss"?
options: An accident in which a worker is badly hurt and taken to hospital
An event that could have caused harm but did not
A tool that is missing from the tool board
A fire drill that started a few minutes late

questions.stem: Why should all accidents and near misses be reported?
options: So that the person involved can be punished
So that the supervisor has more forms to file
So that causes can be found and fixed
So that the workshop can be closed for a week

questions.stem: What is the correct way to lift a box from the floor?
options: Bend your back over it and keep both of your legs straight
Twist your body as you lift to save time
Lift it quickly with a sharp jerk so that it starts to move
Bend your knees, keep your back straight and hold it close

questions.stem: A steel plate is too heavy for one person to lift safely. What should you do?
options: Lift it anyway, but more slowly
Drag it across the workshop floor by one of its corners
Ask a trainee to lift it for you
Get help or use a lifting aid, such as a trolley

questions.stem: Why is good housekeeping (keeping the area clean and tidy) important for safety?
options: It makes the workshop look nice for photos
It means less cleaning is needed at the end
It cuts the risk of trips, slips and fires
It lets tools be left out ready for the next day

questions.stem: How should extension leads and welding cables be run across a work area?
options: Along the edges, or covered, so that people do not trip
Across the middle of the walkway, so they are easy to see
Through puddles of water, so they stay cool
Under doors that are closed on top of them

questions.stem: Where can you find full safety information about a chemical, including first aid and storage?
options: On the price label from the shop
On its safety data sheet (SDS)
In the workshop's attendance book
On the back of the delivery note

questions.stem: Which is safe storage for chemicals such as thinners or cleaning products?
options: In drink bottles, so they are easy to pour
In their labelled containers, in a cool, aired store
Next to the welding bay or the heater, where they are handy
Open on the bench, so that the fumes can escape

questions.stem: Why is good ventilation needed when welding, soldering or using solvents?
options: To keep the work cool so it does not bend
To stop the electricity supply from tripping off during the job
To dry the paint on the walls faster
To remove fumes and vapours that can harm health

questions.stem: How should gas cylinders, such as oxygen and acetylene, be stored?
options: Lying down on the floor, in the sun
Inside a closed cupboard with the heater
Upright and chained, away from heat, in an aired place
Mixed together in any order, in whatever space there is left

questions.stem: When using a ladder, which is safe practice?
options: Keep three points of contact and do not overreach
Stand on the very top rung so that you can reach higher up
Place it on loose boxes to gain extra height
Lean out to the side instead of moving it

questions.stem: A ladder reaches 4 m up a wall. About how far from the wall should its base be?
options: 1 m
2 m
3 m
4 m

questions.stem: Why must guards be kept in place on machines such as grinders and drills?
options: To keep the machine looking clean and new
To make the machine run more quietly
To stop hands, clothing or sparks reaching danger points
To stop other workers from borrowing the machine without asking

questions.stem: Why should long hair be tied back and loose clothing avoided near rotating machines?
options: It makes it harder to see the work clearly
It can be caught and pull the worker in
It may get dusty and need washing more
It can make the worker feel too hot

questions.stem: If you believe a task is unsafe, what should you do?
options: Do it quickly so that the danger is over sooner
Do it, because refusing a task will always get you sacked
Ask a newer trainee to do it instead of you
Stop, and report it to your supervisor before going on

questions.stem: Which is a duty of the worker under good OH&S practice?
options: To buy all the safety equipment for the workshop
To write the health and safety laws for the country
To follow safety rules and use the PPE provided
To repair any machine without permission

questions.stem: Which is a duty of the employer?
options: To pay for each worker's lunch every day
To choose each worker's clothes for home
To make sure that no worker ever takes a break during the day
To provide a safe workplace, training and PPE

questions.stem: Before welding near anything that can burn, what should be done?
options: Remove or cover what can burn and keep an extinguisher ready
Wet the floor so that sparks go out by themselves
Weld very quickly so that the sparks do not have time to spread out
Ask everyone else to leave the building first

questions.stem: When working in Jamaica's heat, how can workers avoid heat stress?
options: Work faster so that the job ends sooner
Drink water often, take breaks in the shade
Take off PPE so that they stay cooler
Drink only sweet energy drinks instead of plain water

questions.stem: Oil has spilled on the workshop floor. What should you do?
options: Walk round it and carry on with your job
Clean it up at once, or fence it off and report it
Cover it with a sheet of cardboard and leave it
Wait for the cleaner to find it some time the next morning

questions.stem: In Jamaica, which number do you call for the fire brigade or an ambulance?
Why do new workers get a safety induction before they start work?
options: So that they can skip reading the safety signs
To show them where the canteen and the parking are found
To check that they have the right phone number
To learn the hazards, rules and emergency procedures

questions.stem: What is the purpose of putting a personal lock and tag on an isolator?
options: To stop the isolator from getting dusty
To show everyone who owns the electrical panel in the building
To stop anyone switching the supply back on while you work
To make the isolator easier to find in the dark

questions.stem: Why are screens put round a welding bay?
options: To keep the welding rods dry
To make the welding bay look neat and tidy for any visitors
To protect people nearby from arc flash and spatter
To stop the welder from taking breaks

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What do the letters "OH&S" stand for?
accepted: occupational health and safety at work

shortAnswers.stem: What colour is a mandatory sign, such as "wear eye protection"?
What colour is a warning sign, such as "danger: high voltage"?
When you smother a small fire with a fire blanket, which part of the fire triangle do you take away?
What do the letters "PPE" stand for?
What instrument is used to prove that an electrical circuit is dead before work starts?
What is the name of the painful eye injury caused by looking at a welding arc without the correct filter?
What is the name of the written approval needed before welding or cutting is done in an area where it is not normally allowed?
What do we call a person at work who is trained to give first aid?
To get away from smoke in a fire, should you stand up tall or keep low?
What three letters are used for the safety device that cuts off the supply quickly when current leaks to earth?
What three letters name the first aid of chest presses and rescue breaths given to a person whose heart has stopped?
What is the name for a planned practice of leaving the building, so that everyone knows what to do in a real fire?
Where are accidents at work written down? Name the book or form.
What word describes a substance that catches fire easily, such as petrol or thinners?

essays.stem: Explain the difference between a hazard and a risk, and describe how to carry out a simple risk assessment for a task in the workshop.
essays.modelAnswer: A hazard is anything that could cause harm, such as a spinning grinder disc, a live cable or a slippery floor. A risk is how likely it is that the hazard will cause harm, and how bad the harm could be. To carry out a risk assessment, first look at the task and the area and list the hazards. For grinding a weld, these are flying sparks and chips, noise, dust and a disc that could break. Next decide who could be harmed: the worker and people nearby. Then judge the risk as low, medium or high. Decide the controls, for example check the disc and guard, use screens, wear a face shield, safety glasses, ear protection and gloves, and keep things that can burn away. Write the findings down, tell the people involved, and review the assessment when something changes.
markingPoints: Correct meaning of hazard, with an example
Correct meaning of risk (likelihood and how bad)
Identify hazards and who may be harmed
Judge the risk and choose controls
Record, tell others and review

essays.stem: Describe the order of controls for a hazard, from the most effective to the least effective, with an example of each.
essays.modelAnswer: The most effective control is elimination: remove the hazard altogether, for example cutting steel to size at the supplier so that there is no cutting in the workshop. Next is substitution: replace the hazard with something less dangerous, such as using a water-based paint instead of one with a strong solvent. Third are engineering controls, which separate people from the hazard: machine guards on a grinder, fume extraction at the welding bay, or an RCD on a power circuit. Fourth are administrative controls, which change the way people work: safety signs, training, a hot work permit, safe work procedures and a rota to limit time in a noisy area. The last control is personal protective equipment, such as a welding helmet, gloves, safety boots and ear protection. PPE comes last because it only protects the wearer and only works if it is worn correctly.
markingPoints: Elimination, with an example
Substitution, with an example
Engineering controls, with an example
Administrative controls, with an example
PPE last, with the reason

essays.stem: Describe the safe isolation procedure to follow before working on an electrical circuit or a machine.
essays.modelAnswer: First identify the correct circuit or machine and the isolator or breaker that supplies it, and tell anyone affected that the supply will be off. Switch off and isolate the supply at the isolator or breaker. Lock it off with a personal lock and keep the key, and fix a tag that says who is working and that it must not be switched on. Next check the voltage tester on a known live source or a proving unit to show that it works. Then test the circuit or machine at the point of work, between all the conductors, to prove that it is dead. Check the tester again on the known source to make sure it did not fail during the test. Only then start work. Never work on live equipment. Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules, and remove the lock only when the work is finished and safe.
markingPoints: Identify the circuit and tell others
Switch off and isolate
Lock off and tag
Prove the tester works, prove dead, then prove the tester again
Never work live; follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules

essays.stem: Describe the actions to take if a fire breaks out in the workshop.
essays.modelAnswer: The first action is to raise the alarm by shouting "Fire!" and setting off the fire alarm, so that everyone knows. Someone should call the fire brigade on 110 and give the address clearly. Only try to put out the fire if it is small, you have been trained, you have the right type of extinguisher and you have a clear way out behind you. If it is safe, switch off the electricity and close the gas cylinder valves. If the fire is too big, or the extinguisher does not work quickly, leave at once by the nearest safe exit. Close doors behind you to slow the fire, but do not lock them. Do not stop to collect your belongings and do not go back inside. Go to the assembly point and take part in the roll call, and tell the fire officers if anyone is missing or if gas cylinders are inside.
markingPoints: Raise the alarm
Call the fire brigade (110)
Fight the fire only if small, trained, right extinguisher and a way out
Switch off power and gas if safe; leave by the nearest safe exit and close doors
Go to the assembly point, roll call, do not go back in

essays.stem: Explain how to choose the right type of fire extinguisher for different kinds of fire.
essays.modelAnswer: The extinguisher must suit what is burning, so always read the label on it, which shows the types of fire it can be used on. Water extinguishers are for fires in solid materials such as paper, wood, cloth and cardboard. They must not be used on electrical equipment, because water conducts electricity, or on burning oil or fuel, because they spread the fire. Foam extinguishers are for burning liquids such as petrol, thinners and paint, and for solids. Carbon dioxide (CO2) extinguishers are for fires in electrical equipment and burning liquids; they leave no mess, but the gas can make the horn very cold and the area can be short of air afterwards. Dry powder extinguishers can be used on many kinds of fire, including electrical, but the powder makes a mess and can make it hard to see. Switch off the power first if it is safe to do so.
markingPoints: Read the label to match the extinguisher to the fire
Water for paper, wood and cloth; never on electrical or oil fires
Foam for burning liquids
CO2 for electrical equipment, with a precaution
Dry powder for many types, with a drawback; switch off power if safe

essays.stem: Describe how to lift and carry a heavy object safely, such as a length of steel or a box of cable.
essays.modelAnswer: First plan the lift. Check the weight, size and shape of the load, and decide whether it can be lifted by one person. If it is too heavy or awkward, get help or use a trolley, a hoist or another lifting aid. Check that the route is clear and that there is space to put the load down. Wear gloves and safety boots. Stand close to the load with feet apart, one slightly forward. Bend the knees and keep the back straight, and get a firm grip. Lift smoothly with the legs, keeping the load close to the body. Do not twist; turn by moving the feet. Make sure you can see over the load. For a long length of steel or a team lift, agree one person to give the commands, and lift and put down together. Put the load down by bending the knees.
markingPoints: Plan: check the load and the route; get help or a lifting aid if needed
Wear gloves and safety boots
Bend the knees, straight back, firm grip, load close
Lift smoothly; do not twist, move the feet
Team lifts: one person gives commands; put down carefully

essays.stem: Describe what you would do if you found a co-worker who had received an electric shock and collapsed.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would not touch the person if they might still be in contact with the electricity, because I could get a shock too. I would switch off the supply at the switch, plug or isolator. If I could not switch it off, I would stand on something dry and push the person or the cable away with a dry piece of wood or another object that does not conduct. Then I would shout for help, send someone to call an ambulance on 110, and call the trained first aider. I would check if the person responds and is breathing. If they are not breathing normally, I would start CPR if I am trained, or follow the instructions of the ambulance call-taker. If they are breathing, I would place them in the recovery position and watch them until help arrives. Afterwards I would cool any burns and make sure the accident is reported.
markingPoints: Do not touch the person while they may be live
Switch off the supply, or use a dry non-conducting object
Shout for help, call 110 and the first aider
Check response and breathing; CPR if trained or recovery position
Treat burns afterwards and report the accident

essays.stem: Explain why accidents and near misses must be reported, and describe what an accident report should include.
essays.modelAnswer: Accidents and near misses must be reported so that the cause can be found and fixed before someone else is hurt. A near miss is a warning that the same thing could cause an injury next time. Reports also make sure the injured person gets the right care, give a record for the employer and any insurance claim, and help the workplace meet its legal duties. A report should be written as soon as possible, while the facts are fresh. It should include the date, time and exact place; the name of the injured person and any witnesses; what the person was doing; what happened, in the order it happened; the injury and the first aid given; the equipment or materials involved; and what has been done to make the area safe. It should stick to facts, not blame, and be signed and handed to the supervisor.
markingPoints: Find and fix causes so it does not happen again
Near misses are warnings
Record for care, insurance and legal duties
Contents: date, time, place, names, witnesses, what happened, injury and first aid
Written promptly, factual, signed and handed to the supervisor

essays.stem: Describe good housekeeping in a workshop, and explain how it helps prevent accidents.
essays.modelAnswer: Good housekeeping means keeping the work area clean, tidy and well organised all the time, not only at the end of the day. Tools are put back in their places after use, so that they are easy to find and nobody trips over them. Walkways and exits are kept clear. Cables and hoses are run along the edges or covered. Offcuts, stubs and scrap metal are put in the right bins, and sharp offcuts are not left on benches. Spills of oil, water or chemicals are cleaned up at once. Rags with oil or solvent are kept in a metal bin with a lid. Materials are stacked safely and not too high. Good housekeeping prevents slips, trips and falls, cuts from sharp metal, and fires from sparks landing on rubbish. It also makes it easier to escape in an emergency.
markingPoints: Tools put away and walkways and exits kept clear
Cables run safely; spills cleaned at once
Scrap, stubs and oily rags in the right bins
Materials stacked safely
Explains how it prevents slips, trips, cuts and fires

essays.stem: Explain the main health and safety duties of the employer, and the main duties of the worker.
essays.modelAnswer: The employer must provide a safe place of work, with safe machines, tools and electrical installations that are checked and maintained. They must carry out risk assessments and put controls in place. They must provide the correct PPE free of charge, and give workers training, information and supervision so that they can work safely. They must provide first aid, fire equipment, safe exits and emergency procedures, and clean toilets and drinking water. They must record and look into accidents. The worker must take care of their own safety and that of others affected by their work. They must follow the safety rules and procedures, wear and look after the PPE provided, and use machines only as trained. They must not misuse or interfere with safety equipment. They must report hazards, faults, near misses and accidents to the supervisor, and stop work and report it if a task is unsafe.
markingPoints: Employer: safe workplace, equipment and maintenance
Employer: risk assessment, PPE, training and supervision
Employer: first aid, fire safety, welfare and accident records
Worker: care for self and others, follow rules, wear PPE
Worker: do not misuse safety equipment; report hazards and stop unsafe work

practical1.title: Workplace hazard inspection and risk assessment
practical1.brief: As a group, inspect one work area at the Centre that the assessor chooses, such as the welding shop or the electrical lab, while it is not in use, and write a risk assessment for it. Use the inspection checklist to look at walkways and exits, cables and leads, machine guards, gas cylinders, chemicals and their labels, fire extinguishers (type, gauge and service tag), the first aid kit, safety signs, lighting, ventilation and housekeeping. Look and point only: do not switch on, open or move equipment. Each member finds and records at least two hazards, photographs each one, and writes on the risk assessment form who could be harmed, the risk (low, medium or high) and a sensible control. The group then agrees which three hazards are most urgent and writes a short report to the supervisor. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in the checklist, the risk assessment form and the report once for the whole group.
materials: A phone or camera for the photos
Safety boots, safety glasses and other PPE the area's rules require
photos: The group in the PPE the area requires, before entering
Each hazard found, with the member who found it pointing to it (at least two per member)
The fire extinguishers and first aid kit, showing the gauge, tag or contents checked
The completed risk assessment form, clear enough to read
The short report listing the three most urgent hazards
checklist: Wore the PPE the area requires and followed the area's rules
Found at least two real hazards and recorded them correctly
Named who could be harmed by each hazard
Gave a sensible risk rating for each hazard
Suggested a control that follows the order of controls
Checked an extinguisher or the first aid kit correctly
Helped write the report and could explain it to the assessor
safety: Inspect only when the area is not in use and the assessor is present
Do not switch on, open, move or touch machines, panels, cylinders or chemicals
Keep to walkways and wear the PPE the area requires; follow the Centre's rules

practical2.title: Emergency response: evacuation drill and basic first aid
practical2.brief: As a group, plan and carry out an evacuation drill for your work area with the assessor, and then show basic first aid steps on each other. Part 1: draw a simple floor plan of the area showing the exits, the alarm point, the fire extinguishers, the first aid kit and the route to the assembly point. Give each member a role: raising the alarm, making the (pretend) call to 110, switching off power and gas at the main points if safe (the assessor confirms; in the drill, point to them only), checking that the area is empty, and taking the roll call at the assembly point. Carry out the drill, timing how long it takes. Part 2: each member, working on a partner, shows how to cool a pretend burn on the arm under cool running water (explaining that this should last about 20 minutes), and how to place a person in the recovery position. Finally, the group writes a short drill report: the time taken, what went well and what to improve. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical.
materials: Paper, ruler and pens for the floor plan
A roll call list of the group
A sink with running water and paper towels
A clean mat or blanket for the recovery position
photos: The finished floor plan showing exits, alarm, extinguishers, first aid kit and the route
Members in their roles at the start of the drill
The group at the assembly point with the roll call being taken
Each member cooling a pretend burn under running water (one photo per member)
Each member placing a partner in the recovery position
checklist: Marked the exits, alarm point, extinguishers and first aid kit correctly on the plan
Carried out their drill role correctly and calmly
Walked, did not run, by the planned route to the assembly point
Gave a clear (pretend) emergency call: who, what, where
Showed burn cooling correctly and said it should last about 20 minutes
Placed a partner in the recovery position safely and correctly
Helped write the drill report with at least one sensible improvement
safety: Agree the drill with the assessor and the Centre first, so that other classes are not alarmed; do not set off the real alarm unless the Centre arranges it
Walk, do not run, during the drill; keep stairs and exits clear
Be gentle when moving a partner into the recovery position, and stop if they feel any pain
Wipe up water at the sink at once so that nobody slips
